audit: Independent adversarial re-review of Hidden Monotonicity repairs
verdict: PASS for the focused eight-module semantic repair review. No critical or high-severity finding remains in these modules, no false repaired theorem or hidden/vacuous main premise was found, and the reviewed source-to-model bridges are genuine. This is a diagnostic semantic/type/axiom/source-compilation receipt, not the root clean-closure publication gate.

resolved_original_findings.evidence: The new pointwise differentiable-head support theorem and original-domain Rademacher/prefix-Q arguments remove Strict. Both identically-zero networks and persistent zero gates are admitted. All individual Q derivatives are certified a.e, with a necessary distinction at exceptional points.
Actual affine heads/logit, readout-bias recovery, true head derivatives, canonical readout mass and both shifted partial invariants are now defined and proved.
The linked affine-chunk theorem now proves the actual ungated affine function and complete property bundle.
Actual maximizing-WTA semantics and independent per-node recentering are integrated into the same shared-node Circuit interpreter.
The precise finite pool pair now has recovery, nonnegative-output, monotonicity and convexity theorems.

The current saliency text has the suffix bulk factor; current masks use strict positivity/inactive zero; the eta-zero source remark has been revised. These were manuscript responsibilities, not new Lean-proof changes.

module_verdicts.reviewed_mechanism: layerJac chooses a genuinely maximizing affine branch even at ties. The single-layer touching affine lower bound is explicit. Nonnegative split weights make every downstream selected Jacobian monotone, so the support inequality composes. The scalar support lemma applies Fermat to f(y)-D(y-x) at its actual local minimum; differentiability identifies D with the genuine Frechet derivative. There is no assumed derivative recurrence or circular support definition. Balanced lifting is applied to the support itself, so differentiability of the full pair-input head is not silently required.

Actual split and affine-head functions have explicit global Lipschitz bounds. Rademacher is applied with volume in the original finite-dimensional input space. Both head coordinates are covered by differentiability of one pair-valued Lipschitz map. The backward invariant quantifies all shifts after a single full-measure event. No Strict premise or assumed null zero-preactivation set appears.

append recursively preserves the actual Network layers, with explicit eval-composition and selected-Jacobian-composition equalities. originalTrace_ae_derivative is obtained coordinatewise from actual affine-head derivatives and their exact difference recovery, not assumed. Each minimum is the actual preactivation minus the next appended ReLU prefix. The induction always keeps the original domain Vec a and appends to the prefix. It never pulls an a.e theorem back through a possibly singular activation map. q.value retains the full variable prefix; only q.jacobian freezes the selected trace at the differentiation point. The canonical absolute-tail equality is inherited explicitly.

affine_Q_row_formulas is the all-input algebraic identity for the existing implemented shifted pass. affine_Q_closed_form_ae intersects the actual-Q and actual-original derivative events, then attaches the affine readout. affine_plain_Q_gradients_ae adds actual derivatives of both head functions on a common full-measure set. The pointwise differentiable-head formula intentionally uses selected Q rows without claiming differentiability of every unused Q function; this distinction is necessary and explicitly stated.

The functions are exactly G=rp(splitPlus)+rn(splitMinus)+bp and H=rn(splitPlus)+rp(splitMinus)+bn. Their difference equals (rp-rn)(eval)+(bp-bn). The readout is genuinely ungated, can give negative logits and has no final minimum/Q source. Zero-shift terminal seeds are proved to differentiate these actual heads. The balanced derivative has the required factor 1/2. coefficientRow sign-sum and sign-difference bridge canonical readout parts to literal absolute and signed coefficient rows.

affineChunk is the ungated pair (preP+bp,preN+bn). Recovery is affineLayer, not ReLU. Nonnegativity uses the explicit nonnegative parameter/input assumptions. Exact affine interpolation and ConvexOn do not require nonnegative biases, and their separate lemmas correctly omit that restriction.

finitePool is exactly the finite nonempty sup/erase-sum construction from the source. The bundled theorem includes recovery, positivity, monotonicity and both convexity claims. PoolWinner is a true global maximizing-index predicate; existence is proved; winnerPool forwards both stream coordinates at the same certified maximizing index. It is no longer the previous tautological arbitrary-index equality.

winnerPair compares the two represented differences and forwards an entire pair, with deterministic left tie breaking. poolTreeSplit recursively selects through top-level nested maximum trees, forwarding a real winning leaf argument pair. Non-max arithmetic uses the existing correct split. splitWithPolicy reuses prior-node values and independently chooses pooling/recentering by each appended node index. All-node recovery/nonnegativity and the literal convex-policy compatibility bridge are proved. No unsupported shape claim is made for WTA or recentering.

nonblocking_scope_notes: At a point where only final heads are differentiable, an unused Q function can still have a kink. The repair correctly does not assert every Q derivative at every such point. Zero readout with Q(x)=min(x,0) at zero is an explicit control showing why this distinction must remain in source links.

For affine_Q_closed_form_ae, shifts and readout parameters are fixed before the a.e input quantifier. For affine_ae_backward_invariants, all shifts occur after one common full-measure event. These are the actual printed quantifier orders; no uncountable-intersection step is used.

The arbitrary signed rp/rn theorem affine_Q_closed_form_ae certifies the original-logit derivative and shifted algorithmic identities. Actual plain-head derivative statements additionally require monotone rp/rn; canonical coefficient rows discharge this genuine positivity condition.

Convex and winner finite-pool implementations may choose different common stream levels; winnerPool uses an arbitrary certified maximizing index while poolTreeSplit has deterministic left tie breaking. Both meet the source shared-winning-index semantics, which imposes no unique tie index.

Concrete tensor flattening, end-to-end converter correctness, and the graph-size bound remain outside these eight repairs; current coverage_map marks the CNN/source-size coverage partial. This focused PASS is not an assertion that the whole thesis is completely formalized.

Stale mass/complementarity equation links were reported during this review and the root corrected them to affine_canonical_mass before the final snapshot. Older strict projection-head helper contracts remain valid within their stated scope.

independent_exact_experiment.enumeration: Every two-layer scalar canonical network with weights/biases in {-1,0,1}; every pair x,y in {-1,0,1}^2

independent_exact_experiment.prefix_control: Second Q of ReLU(ReLU(x)) is min(ReLU(x),0)=0, selected derivative zero even on entire negative halfline
independent_exact_experiment.pointwise_scope_control: Zero readout discards unit-ReLU Q=min(x,0); both heads constant at x=0 but Q has one-sided slopes 1 and 0. This is not a counterexample to the new correctly restricted pointwise theorem.
